title: Yellow Rust of Wheat (Puccinia striiformis)
content: Yellow rust is a fungal disease that affects wheat crops, characterized by yellow stripes of pustules on leaves. It thrives in cool, humid temperatures (10-15°C). It reduces photosynthesis and can cause up to 70% yield loss. Prevention includes sowing resistant varieties like HD 2967 or HD 3086. Treatment: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC @ 200 ml or Tebuconazole 250 EC @ 200 ml in 200 liters of water per acre as soon as pustules appear. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer as it promotes fungal growth.
source: ICAR Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research, Disease Management Guide 2025

title: Loose Smut of Wheat (Ustilago nuda)
content: Loose smut is a seed-borne disease of wheat where healthy grains are replaced by black, powdery spore masses. The disease becomes visible only at the heading stage when the entire ear head turns black. To prevent loose smut, treat seeds before sowing with Carboxin (Vitavax) 75 WP @ 2.5 g/kg seed or Carbendazim (Bavistin) 50 WP @ 2 g/kg seed. Solar heat seed treatment during hot summer months (May-June) is also effective for organic farmers. Destroy infected ear heads in paper bags to prevent spore spread.
source: Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) Wheat Sowing Advisories

title: Rice Blast Disease (Magnaporthe oryzae)
content: Rice Blast is one of the most destructive fungal diseases of paddy, causing lesions on leaves (leaf blast), nodes (node blast), and neck of the panicle (neck blast). Leaf lesions are spindle-shaped with grey centers and brown borders. High relative humidity (above 90%) and leaf wetness favor the disease. Management: Avoid excess application of nitrogen. Spray Tricyclazole 75 WP @ 120 g/acre or Isoprothiolane 40 EC @ 300 ml/acre in 200 liters of water. Seed treatment with Thiram or Carbendazim @ 2g/kg seed is recommended.
source: National Rice Research Institute (NRRI) Crop Protection Portal

title: Bacterial Leaf Blight of Rice (Xanthomonas oryzae)
content: Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB) of rice causes drying of leaves and 'kresek' (wilt of seedlings). It starts as water-soaked stripes on leaf tips, turning yellow-grey with wavy margins. It spreads fast during heavy rains, wind, and high temperatures (25-34°C). Prevention: Use balanced fertilizers; split nitrogen applications. Do not clip seedling tips. Treatment: Spray Streptocycline 6 g + Copper Oxychloride 500 g in 200 liters of water per acre. Alternatively, spray fresh cow dung extract 5% for biological control in early stages.
source: ICAR Agricultural Technology Application Research Institute (ATARI)

title: Early Blight of Tomato (Alternaria solani)
content: Early blight is a fungal disease affecting tomato leaves, stems, and fruits. It starts as small, brown-black spots with concentric rings ('target board' appearance) on older leaves. It spreads upward and leads to defoliation, exposing fruit to sunscald. Management: Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops. Maintain space between plants for aeration. Control: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP @ 600 g/acre or Copper Oxychloride 50 WP @ 500 g/acre in 200 liters of water at 10-15 days intervals. Remove lower leaves up to 1 foot height to prevent soil contact.
source: Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) advisory

title: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)
content: PM-KISAN is a central government scheme providing financial support of Rs. 6,000 per year to all landholding farmer families across India. The financial benefit is transferred directly into the bank accounts of farmers in three equal installments of Rs. 2,000 every four months. Eligibility requires cultivable land in the name of the farmer family. Exclusions include institutional landowners, income tax payers, and pension holders above Rs. 10,000/month. Status can be checked on the PM-KISAN portal using Mobile Number or Aadhaar with OTP verification.
source: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
content: PMFBY is a crop insurance scheme protecting farmers against crop loss due to non-preventable natural calamities, pests, and diseases. Premium rates payable by farmers are capped at 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for annual commercial/horticultural crops. The remaining premium is shared equally by Central and State Governments. Farmers must report crop damage within 72 hours via the Crop Insurance App or to local agriculture officers for localized calamities like hailstorm, inundation, or landslide.

title: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Loan Scheme
content: The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme provides farmers with timely credit for cultivation expenses, post-harvest costs, and domestic needs. Loans up to Rs. 3 Lakhs attract an interest rate of 9%, but with a 3% prompt repayment interest subvention, the effective interest rate is reduced to 4%. Collateral-free agricultural loans are available up to Rs. 1.6 Lakhs. Any farmer, tenant farmer, oral lessee, or sharecropper is eligible. Required documents include land records, identity proof (Aadhaar/PAN), bank account details, and crop cultivation proof.
source: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) & NABARD Credit Guidelines

title: Soil Fertility, NPK Ratios and Composting
content: Soil fertility refers to the soil's ability to supply essential nutrients (Nitrogen N, Phosphorus P, Potassium K) to plants. The ideal NPK ratio for general grain crops is 4:2:1. Nitrogen promotes leaf growth, Phosphorus helps roots and flowers, and Potassium strengthens cell walls and disease resistance. Acidic soils (pH < 6.0) require Lime application, while Alkaline soils (pH > 7.5) require Gypsum. To prepare Vermicompost: Layer farm waste, cow dung, and dry leaves in a cool, shaded pit. Introduce earthworms (Eisenia fetida) and keep the pile moist (60% humidity) for 60-90 days.
source: Soil Health Card Scheme & National Center of Organic Farming (NCOF)

title: Drip Irrigation Design and Water Conservation
content: Drip irrigation is a micro-irrigation method that saves water and nutrients by allowing water to drip slowly to the roots of plants, either on the soil surface or directly onto the root zone, through a network of valves, pipes, tubing, and emitters. It reduces water evaporation, runoff, and weed growth. It operates at low pressure (1.0 to 1.5 kg/cm2) and saves up to 50-70% water compared to flood irrigation. Filters (screen or disc) are mandatory to prevent emitter clogging. Regular acid flushing with Hydrochloric Acid (0.5%) removes salt deposits.
source: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) Technical Manual
